title: Seamless slice switchover with persistent-checkpoint validation and automated rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an orchestrated, tenant-slice-aware rollout path for private (VPC) data-plane/runtime upgrades that guarantees zero user-visible downtime and provides a deterministic automated rollback. The approach relies on atomic persistent checkpoints of runtime state (KV caches and active session manifests), checksum-validated snapshot handoff, and quorum-based health validation prior to traffic acceptance. This ticket covers the controller logic, IaC hooks (Terraform module changes to surface drain/replace commands), health probe suite, and the rollback executor that can restore a snapshot and resume traffic to the previous binary within the same slice without cross-tenant disruption.
tasks: Design checkpoint format and storage contract (S3-compatible with versioned object keys and checksum metadata)
Add Terraform resources/outputs for drain annotations and slice-level lifecycle hooks (pre-update, post-update)
Implement controller state machine: PREPARE -> SNAPSHOT -> VALIDATE -> SWITCH -> OBSERVE -> COMMIT, with explicit failure transitions to ROLLBACK
Build synthetic probe runner that exercises a representative prompt set per-tenant and measures latency, correctness, and cache hit rate
Add quorum validator that requires >=N/2+1 healthy replicas in a slice and KV-consistency checks before cutoff of old instances
Integrate rollback executor that (a) halts traffic, (b) rehydrates checkpoint, (c) restores previous runtime image via orchestrator, (d) replays minimal warmup traces
Expose rollout controls in the operator API for canary-percentage, max-concurrent-slices, and circuit-breaker thresholds
Author a runbook for on-call to trigger manual rollback and inspect checkpoint diagnostics
Write unit and e2e tests for snapshot/restore, and simulate partial-network failures in CI chaos job
Create dashboard panels for rollout progress, probe pass rates, snapshot verification failures, and rollback triggers
acceptance_criteria: A full slice upgrade completes without dropping in-flight sessions for 95% of simulated traffic at peak load
If a validation threshold is missed (by probe or quorum), operator automatically initiates rollback and traffic is restored to previous version within configured SLA
Checkpoints contain consistent KV and session manifests that pass checksum validation and can be restored within target window (<= 90s for medium slices)
Terraform module changes provide two outputs: slice_drain_command and snapshot_location and are backward-compatible for existing private deployments
E2E tests simulate node blackhole and confirm rollback path succeeds in CI pipeline
Dashboards and runbook steps are published and linked; on-call runbook tested in staging run
design_notes: Prefer immutable checkpoint objects to avoid partial-write corruption; use object versioning and an atomic marker file when snapshot completes
Avoid synchronous full-dump for large KV; support incremental warm snapshots (delta sequence numbers) and a short-lived WAL replay to reduce restore time
Quorum validator should check three signals: probe success, KV checksum match across replicas, and expected cache warm percentage
Circuit-breaker thresholds initially conservative: latency p95 increase > 30% OR probe failure rate > 5% OR JVM/native OOM event triggers rollback
Operator API must allow manual pinning of slices to image+checkpoint for debugging and partial rollbacks
